title: Single-site consolidated VCF 9.1 architecture and estate migration
prompt:
Build the architecture artifacts and Go implementation for the DAL01 VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 greenfield deployment in this repository. DAL01 is one site and one failure domain, uses the consolidated architecture, has exactly four available hosts, and must stay at the minimum supported host count. Each host supplies 64 physical cores, 1,024 GiB RAM, and 16 TiB protected usable storage. After one host failure and management reservations of 32 cores, 512 GiB RAM, and 8 TiB storage, the design must still provide at least 144 cores, 2,048 GiB RAM, and 32 TiB storage to workloads. There is no second-site or stretched-cluster requirement. The required VLANs, IP spaces, names, estate inventory, and other inputs are fixed in fixtures/scenario.json and fixtures/estate.json.

Before designing, use your own network access to genuinely research currently published Broadcom compatibility, interoperability, and upgrade-path material for the VMware Cloud Foundation, vCenter, ESX, NSX, and management-component versions involved. Record the source title, live URL, access date, and the design or migration fact learned from each source in artifacts/research-sources.md. Do not treat repository fixtures as a substitute for this live research. Research choices are yours; no particular query or URL is required.

Implement package vcfarchitecture and cmd/render so that go run ./cmd/render deterministically writes artifacts/sddc-spec.json and artifacts/migration-plan.json from the fixtures. The first artifact must be a direct SddcSpec object that validates as SddcSpec against specifications/vcf-installer/vcf-installer-openapi.json, pinned from tag 9.1.0.0 of vmware/vcf-api-specs. It must encode a supported VCF 9.1 consolidated design at the supported minimum host count and satisfy the stated single-host-failure capacity, appliance availability, storage-policy, DNS/NTP, VLAN, MTU, and uplink requirements. Use non-production placeholder credentials where the installer schema requires a credential.

The migration plan must validate against schemas/migration-plan.schema.json. It must contain exactly one ordered step for every component in fixtures/estate.json, naming that component and current version, its target component and version, the action, and every gate that controls the step. Use fixtures/compatibility-snapshot.json as the pinned grading authority for supported target combinations, path order, actions, and gate IDs if live sources have changed. Do not modify the pinned installer specification, fixtures, schemas, or verifier. Add table-driven package tests as appropriate and make go test -race ./... pass.
reference_patch_apply: git apply -p1 --directory=files reference_fix.patch (from the seed root)
